answer: In an agent economy, each participant must continuously prove ownership of a unique hardware-bound key by responding to random challenges within a tight latency window that only a real zephyr of local computation can meet. A pearl of accumulated stake is locked and slashed if the agent fails multiple proofs or if peers detect coordinated behavior typical of sybil farms. Attackers cannot cheaply spin up fable identities because the hardware cost and the risk of total stake loss make large-scale fake populations economically prohibitive.
